overview: Heteromodal and paralimbic association cortex — the dorsolateral and medial prefrontal cortex, insula, posterior cingulate/retrosplenial cortex, parahippocampal cortex, and temporal pole. These multimodal regions sit at the top of the cortical hierarchy, integrating inputs across sensory modalities and supporting higher-order cognition: working memory, cognitive control, attention, self-referential thought, and social cognition. They form the cortical hubs of the large-scale cognitive systems.

citations.source: Mesulam M-M (2000) Principles of Behavioral and Cognitive Neurology, 2nd ed. (heteromodal & paralimbic association cortex)
Kandel et al., Principles of Neural Science, 6th ed. (2021), Ch. 67

function: The dorsolateral prefrontal cortex (DLPFC): a core node of the frontoparietal control network supporting working memory, cognitive control, and planning.
Its posterior part contains the frontal eye fields, which direct goal-driven saccades as part of the dorsal attention network.

clinical.note: Lateral prefrontal lesions impair planning, working memory, and cognitive flexibility.
Hypoactivation of the DLPFC during working-memory and inhibitory tasks.

citations.source: Goldman-Rakic PS (1995) Cellular basis of working memory. Neuron 14:477–485.
Miller EK, Cohen JD (2001) An integrative theory of prefrontal cortex function. Annu Rev Neurosci 24:167–202.

function: Lateral superior frontal gyrus forms the upper DLPFC, contributing to working memory and cognitive control.
Its medial surface is part of the medial prefrontal cortex (mPFC), a hub of the default-mode network for self-referential processing and mentalizing.

clinical.note: Medial frontal lesions reduce initiative and spontaneous behavior.
Medial prefrontal over-engagement underlies excessive self-focus and rumination.

citations.source: Northoff G et al. (2006) Self-referential processing in our brain — a meta-analysis. Neuroimage 31:440–457.
Miller EK, Cohen JD (2001) An integrative theory of prefrontal cortex function. Annu Rev Neurosci 24:167–202.

function: The insular cortex, especially its anterior portion, mediates interoception — the conscious awareness of internal bodily states — and is the key hub of the salience network.
Integrates visceral, autonomic, and affective signals to tag stimuli as behaviorally salient and to switch between the default-mode and executive networks.

afferent: Ventromedial posterior nucleus of the thalamus (visceral)

clinical.note: Altered insular interoceptive signaling underlies panic and somatic symptom disorders.
Insular dysfunction links to the misattribution of salience in psychosis.

citations.source: Craig AD (2009) How do you feel — now? The anterior insula and human awareness. Nat Rev Neurosci 10:59–70.
Seeley WW et al. (2007) Dissociable intrinsic connectivity networks for salience processing and executive control. J Neurosci 27:2349–2356.

function: The frontopolar cortex (Brodmann area 10): the most anterior prefrontal region, supporting relational reasoning, prospective memory, and cognitive branching (holding goals in mind while pursuing subgoals).
Contributes to the anterior component of the default-mode network during internally-directed thought.

clinical.note: Impaired multitasking and 'cognitive branching' with otherwise intact routine tasks.

citations.source: Koechlin E, Hyafil A (2007) Anterior prefrontal function and the limits of human decision-making. Science 318:594–598.
Burgess PW, Gilbert SJ, Dumontheil I (2007) Function and localization within rostral prefrontal cortex (area 10). Philos Trans R Soc Lond B 362:887–899.

function: The ventral posterior cingulate cortex (PCC): a core hub of the default-mode network, active at rest and during self-referential thought and autobiographical memory.
Its activity tracks the balance between internally- and externally-directed attention, deactivating during demanding external tasks.

afferent: Anterior nuclei of the thalamus (Papez circuit)

clinical.note: Early PCC/precuneus hypometabolism and amyloid deposition.
PCC–medial prefrontal hyperconnectivity is a robust neuroimaging finding.

citations.source: Buckner RL, Andrews-Hanna JR, Schacter DL (2008) The brain's default network. Ann N Y Acad Sci 1124:1–38.
Raichle ME et al. (2001) A default mode of brain function. Proc Natl Acad Sci USA 98:676–682.

function: The dorsal posterior cingulate / retrosplenial cortex: supports spatial orientation, navigation, and the retrieval of episodic context.
Acts as an interface between hippocampal memory and the default-mode network's self-referential and spatial functions.

clinical.note: Retrosplenial damage impairs navigation and the use of spatial landmarks.

citations.source: Vann SD, Aggleton JP, Maguire EA (2009) What does the retrosplenial cortex do? Nat Rev Neurosci 10:792–802.
Buckner RL, Andrews-Hanna JR, Schacter DL (2008) The brain's default network. Ann N Y Acad Sci 1124:1–38.

function: The middle-posterior cingulate cortex: part of the posterior default-mode core, integrating self-referential, mnemonic, and visuospatial signals.
Contributes to the continuity of the autobiographical self across time.

clinical.note: Posterior default-mode hyperconnectivity associates with rumination.

citations.source: Buckner RL, Andrews-Hanna JR, Schacter DL (2008) The brain's default network. Ann N Y Acad Sci 1124:1–38.

function: The parahippocampal cortex (posterior portion contains the parahippocampal place area, PPA): represents spatial scenes and environmental context.
Its anterior portion feeds the entorhinal cortex, gating episodic encoding into the hippocampus.

afferent: Fusiform and lateral occipitotemporal cortex (visual 'what' stream)

clinical.note: PPA damage impairs recognition of places and scenes.
Entorhinal/parahippocampal involvement produces early topographical and memory deficits.

citations.source: Epstein R, Kanwisher N (1998) A cortical representation of the local visual environment. Nature 392:598–601.
Aggleton JP, Brown MW (1999) Episodic memory, amnesia, and the hippocampal–anterior thalamic axis. Behav Brain Sci 22:425–489.

function: The temporal pole, the anterior tip of the temporal lobe: a paralimbic association region supporting semantic memory, social and emotional concepts, and face/name recognition.
Serves as an amodal 'hub' linking distributed modality-specific semantic representations.

clinical.note: Anterior temporal atrophy produces progressive loss of word and object meaning.
Temporal pole damage impairs naming and the recognition of familiar faces.

citations.source: Patterson K, Nestor PJ, Rogers TT (2007) Where do you know what you know? The representation of semantic knowledge in the human brain. Nat Rev Neurosci 8:976–987.
Olson IR, Plotzker A, Ezzyat Y (2007) The enigmatic temporal pole: a review of findings on social and emotional processing. Brain 130:1718–1731.
